checks.name: api-imports-neither-release-nor-update
checks.summary: the guard parses the package's own non-test .go files with go/ast (parser.ImportsOnly) and fails outright on a zero-file scan, so it cannot pass vacuously; logged 'api import guard scanned 3 non-test files and 28 import paths'. It follows the verified-matcher idiom of internal/release/source_guard_test.go: four known-positive paths (internal/release, internal/release/sub, internal/update, internal/update/sub) must be detected, and five known-negative paths (net/http, internal/application, internal/domain, internal/releasenotes, internal/updater) must not be, which also pins that the matcher compares whole path segments. The positive control goes further than the matcher: a synthetic source file that really does import internal/release is parsed and asserted to be flagged by the scan itself. The forbidden paths are assembled from two string fragments on purpose, because a single literal holding the full module path would be read by ci/components.json's dependency derivation as an api -> release literal edge and would invert the very guard it is assertion data for; internal/ci's LiteralFalsePositives table is the only other place that could record it and internal/ci is not this task's to edit. Independently confirmed with go list: internal/api's Imports, TestImports and XTestImports contain neither internal/release nor internal/update.

checks.summary: exactly one route was added, GET /v1/release/state, on the existing owner GET seam (authenticate, require application.RoleOwner, put the caller in the context with application.ContextWithCaller, delegate to the Service). Asserted: 401 unauthenticated; 403 for the runner role; 405 for POST, PUT, DELETE and PATCH, with the method check first, following the /healthz idiom, so a POST is a method error rather than a 404; 503 with error code release_observer_not_configured and the standard envelope (error, message, schema_version, correlation_id) when no observer is configured, and the 503 body is asserted to carry no release_version, bundle_digest, conditions or promotable key. Asserted no promote, rollback or set-preview route exists: POST to /v1/release/promote, /v1/release/rollback, /v1/release/preview, /v1/release/state:promote and /v1/release/state:rollback all return 404, and GET on none of them returns 200.

checks.name: component-edge
checks.summary: component edge measured effect. ci/components.json gained exactly one declaration: component application's dependencies now lists release, and nothing else in that file changed (git diff: 2 insertions, 1 deletion, the deletion being the reflowed closing bracket of the dependencies array). The declaration and the real non-test import are in the same commit, because ci.VerifyNoUnjustifiedEdges rejects a declared edge that is not derived from any import, literal or check target. ci/key-closure.json was regenerated with devbox run --pure -- make key-closure and git diff --exit-code on it is clean afterwards. Measured consequence, wider than 'application and api': seven component closures changed, api, application, control-plane, reconciler, runner, store-firestore and store-memory, because every one of them depends transitively on application. Each of those seven now hashes internal/release/**, and the five that did not already reach contracts also gained contracts/**, contracts/release-contract/** and contracts/schemas/release-contract.json. The accepted side effect is that a contract or release edit now invalidates those component keys, which is what V2-045 intended: selective CI must select application and api when internal/release changes.
